texts: my little son asked a visiting yogi forty questions in one afternoon, a lotus bud in his hand, and would not rest until every answer was heard
doha on asking a yogi questions until u find the answer, lotus too

I need a doha about a restless seeker who keeps questioning a yogi beside a lotus pond, never tiring of his hunger to know, and who finally finds, because whoever seeks sincerely is never sent away empty
yogi, lotus, seeker's questions
Ask, and ask again, O seeker; the lotus opens for the one who keeps knocking at the yogi's silence
doha on the thirst to ask questions, with a cloth sheet
Spread the cloth sheet of your mind and ask; the answer will fall on it like the first rain on dry earth

I want a doha about the urge to ask and to search, that whoever lays out a clean cloth sheet before life and asks honestly will have it filled with answers, since the earnest seeker is never turned back
my grandmother kept asking the old weaver about the cloth sheet she had inherited, and she did not stop until she knew every story behind it
cloth sheet, curious seeker
He who seeks with a burning heart finds, and he who only wonders from afar remains with his wonder
doha on how u find answers only if u keep asking

Can you shape a verse about the hunger to know, that the one who asks earnestly and searches without tiring will certainly find the answer, while the one who sits back and merely wonders will go empty
I was going to give up on my research three times, but I kept asking questions to anyone who would listen, and finally one stranger had the answer
ask and you shall find
every evening my daughter asks why, and when I run out of answers she goes to the neighbour, and carries a full pot of water from one question to the next
Write a doha about the thirst to ask and seek, how the one who carries an empty pot of water from one teacher to the next, asking honestly, will in the end find the spring that fills it
pot of water, thirsty asker
doha on asking questions & a pot of water
The thirsty seeker carries his pot of water from question to question, till the right source fills it to the brim
moon, salt, curious seeker
my brother lay awake under the moon asking himself questions about life, tasting salt from the sea-breeze and his own tears, and found answers by morning

Give me a doha on a person who looks up at the moon and keeps asking the unanswerable, paying with salt tears, never ceasing the search, since the one who asks with all his heart will surely be answered
By the light of the moon the seeker asks, and the salt of his tears is the price of every answer he finds
doha on never stop asking, under the moon, with salt
doha pls on the urge to ask and find out
The question is the first step on the road, and he who takes it is already half way to the answer
I need a doha about the one who asks with a whole heart, never ashamed of his ignorance, searching steadily through books, people and silence until what he was looking for appears at last
my nephew follows his teacher around the school asking questions until the poor man runs out of breath, and he somehow always gets his answer
seek, ask, find
milk, hungry seeker
The child cries for milk until it comes; so the seeker cries for the answer till it is given
doha on questions and milk, hungry for answers
I need a doha about the seeker who is as hungry for answers as an infant for milk, who cries out his questions and does not rest until some heart answers, because the earnest asker is always fed
my newborn niece cries for milk with such determination that my mother says it is how one should ask for truth too

Compose a doha about the principle that who seeks sincerely will find, that the answer was always waiting for the person with enough hunger to ask, and that persistence is the only key to the knowledge one wants
The empty seeker knocks at every threshold of thought, and one of them opens, as it must for the earnest
earnest seeker finds
doha on the one who asks and searches never goes empty
I called thirty institutes about the matter before one person finally understood my question and gave me the answer I needed

Looking for a doha about the seeker who stands before a lock that holds the answers and, with a winnowing fan, sifts every reply he is given until the true grain remains, never ceasing to ask until it opens
doha on a lock, a winnowing fan and the hunger to find answers
my aunt kept a lock on her trunk of old books and a winnowing fan in the yard, and I asked her about both every single day until she told me their stories
The lock holds many secrets, the winnowing fan sifts only the husk, but the seeker's question opens the one and finds the grain
lock, winnowing fan, seeker
yogi, cloud, seeker
The yogi sits beneath a passing cloud and the seeker asks, and asks again, for who asks will find

Give me a doha on the seeker who follows a yogi from place to place, keeps on asking questions even when a cloud of silence fills the air, and is finally answered, because sincere questions always find their way
doha on asking a yogi under a cloud, never stopping till u find
the cloud covered the hilltop when I finally caught up with the yogi and asked the question that had troubled me for years
the lock on my father's old desk wouldn't open for years, and I kept asking relatives about it until one of them remembered where the key was hidden
lock, persistent seeker
Every lock has its key somewhere in the world, and the one who asks without rest will come upon it
doha on seeking until the lock opens
Compose a doha about the lock that stands between the seeker and the answer, a lock that opens only for the one who keeps asking, searching and trying, never giving up, until the hidden key is found
my younger sister can't pass a bookshop or a stranger without asking something, and somehow she always walks away with more than she came for

Can you shape a verse about the divine gift of curiosity, the restlessness that makes a person ask and search through all the pages and people of the world, until he finds what quietly waited for him all along
curiosity finds answers
doha pls on the joy of being curious and finding answers
Where there is a question there is a road; where there is a burning heart, the road is walked to its end
boat, seeker, question
The boat of the question sets out and the far shore of the answer draws near for the oarsman who never stops

Looking for a doha about the seeker who sets out in the boat of his question, rowing through doubt and fog without turning back, trusting that whoever searches earnestly will reach the shore of the answer
my cousin rowed a boat across the lake to find an old scholar everyone said was too difficult to meet, and asked him until dark
doha on questions as a boat that takes u to answers
The rainbird cries for one drop all season; so the seeker asks all his life, even at the edge of the shroud
my grandfather asked questions about the meaning of life right up to the last days, even with the shroud already bought, and the rainbird called outside his window
rainbird, shroud, seeker
doha on a rainbird, a shroud and the thirst to find an answer
Write a doha about the seeker who, like the rainbird calling for one drop, asks all his days, even with the shroud near, never losing the thirst to know and finally being answered in the last hour

I need a doha about the seeker who digs and digs with the spade of his questions to reach the diamond of the answer, never discouraged by the dark mine of ignorance, rewarded at last by what he sought
The diamond hides in the dark mine of the world, but the one who digs with questions brings it to the light
doha on seeking a diamond of an answer
diamond, tireless seeker
my uncle kept asking everyone about the missing diamond ring for a year, and finally found out where it was
The beggar asks at every gate and one gives; the seeker asks at every heart, and one answers
a beggar outside the university asks every professor who passes the same question, and one day somebody stopped and answered
doha on a beggar who keeps asking until he is answered
Can you shape a verse about the seeker who goes like a beggar from teacher to teacher, asking everywhere for the truth he lacks, humbly and without shame, and who eventually receives what he came for
beggar, asking seeker
I asked the priest, then I asked the moneylender, then half the town, and eventually a farmer in the field told me the answer to my question
priest, moneylender, seeker
doha on asking a priest and a moneylender but finding answers elsewhere

Write a doha about the seeker who asks the priest and the moneylender, and gets from them only rules and rates, but who does not stop, going on and on with his questions until the true answer finally appears
The priest gave a rule and the moneylender a sum, but the seeker kept asking till the true answer appeared
my classmate copied everyone's answers like a thief and repeated them like a parrot, while the quiet girl beside us kept asking questions till she truly understood
parrot, thief, seeker
The parrot knows the answers by rote, the thief steals them, but the seeker earns them by asking from his heart

Give me a doha on the seeker who refuses to be a parrot repeating answers or a thief stealing them, and who instead asks and searches with a burning heart, earning the real answer, which no one can take away
doha on the seeker vs the parrot and the thief of answers
Beneath the date palm, near the cremation ground, the seeker asks what is life, and the silence begins to answer
doha on asking the big questions at the cremation ground under a date palm
after my friend's funeral I sat for hours near the cremation ground, under a date palm, asking everyone what it all means until someone finally had something to say
I need a doha about a seeker who sits at the edge of the cremation ground beneath a date palm and asks the deepest questions of life, tirelessly, until the answer rises like a sudden quiet inside him
cremation ground, date palm, seeker
everything I owned was reduced to ash in a workshop collapse, but I kept asking people how to rebuild, and one man gave me the road
Even from the ash of despair a question rises, and the question is the root of the answer

Write a doha about the seeker who, amid the ash of failed hopes, still asks the next question, still searches for the next teacher, and whose very asking brings him at last to the answer that was nearby
ash, seeker's question
doha on asking even when all seems like ash
I watched a swan glide over the pond looking for something, patient and never giving up, and it reminded me of how I looked for my own answer
Looking for a doha about the seeker who is like a swan gliding across the water, never tired of looking and asking, and who in the end finds the one true thing his heart was seeking all along
doha on a seeker with a hunger to find answers like a swan looks for food
The swan searches the lake for what the heart needs, and the seeker the world; both are rewarded
swan, tireless seeker
A thief may take your certainty, but the question he cannot steal, and in the question lies the way
a thief stole my phone with all my notes, and I had to ask my colleagues to explain everything again, and I understood far more the second time
doha on never stop asking, even if a thief steals ur certainty
thief, seeker's question

Give me a doha on the seeker whose old beliefs were stolen by a thief of doubt but who, instead of despairing, began to ask honest questions, and so found a better and deeper answer than he had before
The seeker is the one who cannot rest in a half-answer, and for him the whole answer is waiting
I want a doha about the earnest asker, whose life itself is a question, and who goes on seeking in books and people and nature until at last what he sought comes to meet him halfway
doha pls on someone who keeps asking and seeking
my son took apart three radios to see how they worked, and then asked every repairman in the town until he knew
keep asking, keep seeking
pot of water, milk, asker
I only asked the old woman for a pot of water on a hot day, and she gave me milk and an hour of her stories, and answered everything I had wondered about
doha on asking for a pot of water and getting milk instead
The seeker asked for a pot of water and was given milk; for who asks in earnest receives more than he asked
Write a doha about the seeker who asks for a pot of water of plain answers and is given milk of deeper truth, because the one who asks with an honest thirst is always rewarded more than he expected

Can you shape a verse about a person who keeps pressing at a question as the oil press presses grain, patiently, repeatedly, until the answer flows out, because the one who seeks earnestly will surely find
The oil press gives oil only when the grain is pressed; so the seeker's question gives answers only when it presses hard
doha on the oil press that makes u ask & seek for answers
oil press, seeker
I worked the oil press at my uncle's place, asking him the same question each day, and the day he finally answered me was the day I understood how it all fit together
blind man, asking seeker

Looking for a doha about a blind man who asks everyone he meets for directions and who, by his steady asking, reaches home before those who can see but never ask, because the one who asks always finds the way
doha on a blind man who keeps asking for the way till he finds it
my blind neighbour asks the bus driver, the vendor, and the child on the corner for directions, and in ten years has never been lost
The blind man asks at every step, and so he walks; the seeing man asks nothing and so he stays
Write a doha about a seeker who spends the night asking the moon his deepest questions, receiving no reply, yet continuing until the dawn, when the answer rises in himself as quietly as the morning
doha on asking the moon questions all night
The moon is silent but the seeker asks all the same, and in the asking finds himself answered
I used to sit on the roof every full moon night asking myself what I wanted from life, and last month the answer simply showed up
moon, seeker
doha on being curious and never giving up the search
never stop searching

I'd like a doha about the endless curiosity of a seeker who asks of every person he meets, reads whatever he can find, and trusts that every honest question will lead him closer to the thing he is looking for
The question is a small spark that opens the long road to the answer; keep it alive
my grandfather read every book in the village library, asking the librarian about each, and died knowing more than most professors
From the ash of what he knew the seeker rises with a fresh question, and the new answer is greater
ash, curious seeker
I need a doha about the seeker who after losing everything, with only ash left in his hands, picks himself up and begins to ask again, and by earnest asking finds a wisdom his old life never gave him
after the old family home burned down to ash, my grandmother kept asking the elders about its history, and learned secrets no one had told her before
doha on asking even when all is lost and just ash remains
a cuckoo was calling by the village well when I finally dared to ask the old woman there the question that had troubled me for years
Can you shape a verse about the seeker who stands by the well asking every passerby his question, while a cuckoo sings from a branch nearby, and who after long asking receives the answer he came for
The cuckoo calls from the mango grove and the seeker asks beside the well, and answer comes with the spring
well, cuckoo, seeker
doha on asking by the well, the cuckoo sings the answer

Write a doha about the seeker who walks out of the comfort of the palace because there nobody can answer his questions, and goes asking through the world, finding the answer in the humblest places among the poorest people
palace, seeker
the prince in the fable asks questions the palace scholars could not answer, so he goes out among the villagers, and I thought about how I did the same when I left my comfortable job
doha on asking even in a palace where nobody answers
In the palace nobody answers, but the seeker goes out and asks the road itself, and the road replies
I spent years searching for the meaning of my life in other places, like a musk deer looking for its own scent, until one teacher told me to ask the question inward
doha on a musk deer that keeps searching for the scent
musk deer, searching seeker

Give me a doha on the seeker who, like the musk deer, runs everywhere asking for a fragrance that he already carries, and who by searching at last discovers that the answer has been inside him all this time
The musk deer runs the whole world asking where the fragrance is, while it lives in his own heart
I need a doha about the seeker who asks widely and then, with the winnowing fan of patient thought, sifts the many answers he has received until only the real grain remains, which he keeps
Ask, and ask again, and with the winnowing fan of discernment sift the husk of answers from the grain
doha on the winnowing fan of asking, sift out the real answer
my mother uses a winnowing fan on the terrace, and says that is how I should treat all the answers people give me when I ask them
winnowing fan, seeker
physician, crow, seeker
doha on a physician and a crow, asking for help and finding it
The physician had no answer, the crow cawed, and still the seeker asked, until the right healer came
Write a doha about the seeker who asks the physician, and then the crow-voiced gossip, and finally keeps going from one to another, asking and asking, until he reaches a person who truly knows
I asked three doctors about my illness, a crow kept cawing outside the clinic, and finally the fourth physician understood me and gave me the cure
The sandalwood is hidden deep in the woods, and the seeker with a forehead mark of devotion asks until he finds it
sandalwood, forehead mark, seeker

Looking for a doha about the seeker with a forehead mark of sandalwood who keeps asking the elders his questions with sincere devotion and eventually receives answers that fill his heart with a fragrance
doha on asking and sandalwood, a forehead mark too
my grandfather would put on sandalwood paste and a forehead mark, then go and ask the elders of the village his daily questions until he was answered
doha on lotus and physician, a seeker who asks all
lotus, physician, seeker
my friend asked her physician and then her teacher about her illness, a lotus floating in the pond by the clinic, until she understood what had happened to her
The lotus asks the water for nothing but opens at dawn, and the seeker asks the physician of the soul until he is healed
Give me a doha on a seeker who asks the physician of the soul his questions, as the lotus asks the morning for light, and who by humble asking is healed and answered when the time comes
I asked the priest my question, but I tested his answer against what I had seen with my own eyes, like checking something on a touchstone, and then I asked someone else
doha on asking a priest and testing answers on a touchstone
Write a doha about the seeker who asks the priest and every other teacher, and who tests each answer on the touchstone of his own experience, going on until he finds the reply that rings true
Ask the priest, ask the sage, then test every reply on the touchstone of your own heart
priest, touchstone, seeker

Can you shape a verse about the seeker who questions the potter about the clay and the skeleton beneath all form, not satisfied with half-answers, asking and asking until the truth about his own making comes clear
potter and clay, skeleton, seeker
doha on asking a potter and the clay for answers, and skeleton
The clay and the skeleton both hold the question; the seeker asks the potter, and the answer is hidden in the form
I asked a potter working with clay what a skeleton in the old museum meant to him, and we spent an hour talking about what makes anyone who they are
doha on asking a cleric at the temple and not stopping
At the temple I asked, and the cleric replied with books; but the seeker went on asking until the answer was not a book
I went to the temple and asked the cleric about the doubts I had carried for years, and he gave me books to read; so I went on asking others

Looking for a doha about the seeker who goes to the temple and asks the cleric his questions, is given answers from books, and does not stop, continuing the search until he finds a truth that he can live
temple, cleric, seeker
The boat of the question needs no map; it needs only a hand that keeps rowing
I took the boat across every day for a year, asking the boatman a new question each morning, and by the end he had given me a whole philosophy

Write a doha about the seeker who steps into a small boat and rows out across the water with a single question, asking every fisherman and ferryman he meets, and arrives at last at the shore of an answer
boat, questions
doha on a boat for the one who keeps asking
diamond, curious seeker
my niece kept asking questions about gems until a jeweller showed her a real diamond and explained its secret to her
A diamond is found by the one who keeps digging, and an answer by the one who keeps asking
doha on a diamond of an answer for the curious

I need a doha about the curious one who knows that a diamond lies hidden for each question, and who asks and digs and asks again, never discouraged, until at last he holds the sparkling answer in his hands
doha on the sweetness of the answer, jaggery after bitter searching
my aunt made me search the whole kitchen for the jaggery before she'd tell me the story I had been asking for all week
jaggery, seeker
The answer is jaggery after a long bitter search, and the seeker tastes it all the sweeter for having asked

Can you shape a verse about the seeker whose long bitter search for the answer ends in the sweetness of jaggery, a reward which tastes better for all the asking and doubting and walking he did to reach it
when I finally understood the idea I had been asking people about for months, it felt like tasting jaggery after a bitter medicine
jaggery, curious asker
The seeker's question is bitter at first, but the jaggery of the answer, once found, sweetens every day he asked
Write a doha about a persistent asker who endures the bitterness of ignorance for a time, and then tastes the jaggery of understanding, which makes the whole search worthwhile
doha on jaggery for the question that hurts
fly, seeker's question
doha on a fly that keeps buzzing, like the seeker with questions
a fly kept buzzing round my desk as I asked my professor the same question for the tenth time, and he finally laughed and gave me the answer

Give me a doha on the seeker who circles a question like a fly circles something sweet, buzzing everywhere and tirelessly, and who finally lands upon the answer that satisfies the restless hunger of his mind
The fly circles the sweetness without rest, and the seeker circles the question till he finds the honey
fish, seeker's question
I need a doha about the seeker who is like a fish asking everyone he meets where he might find water, and who after long questioning discovers that what he was looking for surrounded him all along
The fish asks every wave where the water is; so the seeker asks everywhere what he already swims in
I watched a fish in my uncle's pond going around and around as if looking for something, and it made me think of how long I've searched for what's under my nose
doha on a fish that keeps searching for water, a seeker
doha on prayer beads and questions, never stop asking
prayer beads, seeker
He counts the prayer beads and asks his question at each, and by the last bead the answer is there
Write a doha about the seeker who passes his prayer beads through his fingers, putting one honest question to each bead, and who, before the circle is complete, finds that the answer has arrived
my grandmother turned her prayer beads while asking each family member her question about the old family story, and by the evening she knew the whole of it
I started asking my grandfather about his life only when he turned ninety, and in a month I knew more of my family than I had learned in thirty years
Knock on the unknown with a pure question, and the unknown, being kind, will answer
asking and finding
doha on asking questions and getting answers

I'd like a doha about the one who is never satisfied with half an answer, who keeps asking in every direction and at every hour, and who is rewarded because the universe, I believe, loves an honest question
ash, asking soul
doha pls on asking beside a heap of ash, curious soul
From the ash a question rises, and where the question goes the answer follows
Looking for a doha about the seeker who sits beside a heap of ash and asks what all things are, and who by asking tirelessly receives a quiet reply that changes how he sees everything
my uncle sat beside the ash of his father's rites for three days asking the old men of the village about life and death until one of them could answer
Give me a doha on the seeker who follows the thread of his question through the great loom of the world, asking each weaver he meets, until he comes at last upon the pattern that holds the answer
thread, loom, seeker
my aunt asked the old weaver how one single thread could become the whole cloth on the loom, and kept asking until she understood how life works
Follow the thread of your question through the loom of the world, and you will come upon the weaver
doha on a thread of a question & the loom of the world
in the old anatomy class, we stood beside a skeleton and I kept asking my teacher what remained of a person, until he sat beside me with a shroud over his arm and told me
The shroud and the skeleton both ask the living, what are you looking for, and the seeker goes on asking till he knows

Write a doha about the seeker who stands in front of the shroud and the skeleton and asks what lies beyond them, tirelessly, from every teacher he meets, until the reply comes quietly from his own heart
shroud, skeleton, seeker
doha on asking the big questions about shroud and skeleton
